name: Macedonian nationalism
summary: Macedonian nationalism holds that ethnic Macedonians are a distinct Slavic nation, separate from Bulgarians, Serbs and Greeks, with their own language, church and state. It grew from late-19th-century cultural and political thought (Misirkov, Ilinden) into the Yugoslav republic and the independent state of 1991. Its modern mainstream, represented by VMRO-DPMNE, stresses national identity, the Macedonian Orthodox Church and sovereignty, resisting Greek, Bulgarian and Albanian demands, while pursuing EU and NATO membership and formally disclaiming territorial claims.
scope: The mainstream post-1991 nationalism of the Macedonian state as expressed by VMRO-DPMNE and the heritage it invokes (Krste Misirkov's 1903 On Macedonian Matters, Ilinden and Kruševo, ASNOM, the 1991 constitution). Excludes the irredentist 'United Macedonia' fringe and diaspora 'ancient descent' fundamentalism, which are noted but not treated as typical. Economic and social answers are mostly inferred from the centre-right, Christian-democratic party that carries the movement.

keyFigures.name: Krste Misirkov
keyFigures.role: Author of On Macedonian Matters (1903), advocate of a separate Macedonian people and standard language.

keyFigures.name: Nikola Gruevski
keyFigures.role: VMRO-DPMNE leader and prime minister 2006-2016 who pursued antiquization and Skopje 2014.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred: the party that carries this nationalism is centre-right, but the constitution (Art. 8) commits to social justice and public health care is not contested by adherents.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from centre-right VMRO-DPMNE's populist wage promises; the sources do not discuss wage policy, so this is a weak lean.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred: Art. 8 and 55 guarantee free markets and entrepreneurship, and the leading nationalist party is centre-right, but economics is not core to the nationalism.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred: VMRO-DPMNE governments privatised heavily (per the IMF-cited criticism), so adherents lean against public ownership of major industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party's low-tax, investment-attracting approach; the sources do not state a nationalist position on taxation.

unions-good.rationale: The movement has no stated labour position; nationalists are split between populist-left and market-friendly attitudes.

property-fundamental.rationale: The constitution (Art. 8, 59) protects property and foreign investors' rights, so adherents lean towards strong property protection, though this is not a nationalist theme.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Art. 55 requires action against monopolies, but nationalism itself says little on corporate regulation, so adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: the constitution lists social justice among its values and the movement is not an anti-welfare one.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: a party with an anti-communist founding and an insider-favouring privatisation record is unlikely to back worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the 2015 wiretapping scandal under VMRO-DPMNE rule suggests tolerance, but adherents are not documented as taking a side.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative, Christian-democratic self-description of the main nationalist party.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed in sources; nationalists see themselves as targets of hate speech from neighbours but do not seek speech laws as a program.

strong-leader.rationale: Gruevski-era authoritarian tendencies are documented, but the movement's founding texts are not leader-centred, so adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement is state-building: the constitution and Ilinden heritage centre on a sovereign state, so rejecting the state is alien to it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; no documented nationalist position on gun ownership.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from the stress on defending a small state against neighbours' claims and on the 2001 conflict, though not stated in the sources.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the conservative, Christian-democratic positioning of the main nationalist party.

decide-locally.rationale: The 1990s nationalist line wanted a unitary nation-state; decentralisation arrived via Ohrid and is associated with minority demands.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no documented adherent position.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: VMRO-DPMNE rebranded as Christian-democratic and conservative, and the Orthodox church is a pillar of the movement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the conservative Christian-democratic outlook of the main nationalist party and the Orthodox church's role.

abortion-legal.rationale: Conservative Orthodox sentiment pulls against, but abortion is legal in the country and not a nationalist issue, so adherents are split.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Macedonian Orthodox Church is described as a main cultural pillar of the movement, so a larger public role for it is favoured; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's own grievance is national, not racial.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from social conservatism of the main nationalist party; not addressed in sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving Macedonian language, church and heritage against Greek, Bulgarian and Serbian assimilation is the movement's defining purpose, and Art. 49 protects the Macedonian people's heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was itself a radical break from older identities, but today it defends existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; North Macedonia is chiefly a country of emigration and the movement's concern is the diaspora and Albanians, not immigrants.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: the party has moved to soft Euroscepticism out of fear of identity concessions imposed from outside.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's free-market and foreign-investor guarantees (Art. 55, 59).

nation-first.rationale: Defending Macedonian identity against concessions demanded by Greece, Bulgaria and the EU is a core theme of VMRO-DPMNE, which called the Prespa deal a betrayal of national interests.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no documented stance.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred: a nationalism concerned with preserving a small nation's character does not favour open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: the main nationalist party stresses growth and unemployment reduction.

revolution-justified.rationale: Ilinden and the Kruševo Republic are celebrated as founding uprisings against Ottoman rule, but modern adherents defend an established state, so they are split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from the party's populist turn under Mickoski and its distrust of elites who made concessions.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from the party's anti-communist origin and market orientation.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from the same anti-communist, pro-market orientation; not stated.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party's economic outlook.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right economic outlook; not addressed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between investment-attracting openness and protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The party's governments subsidised foreign investors in zones, but the nationalism has no stated industrial policy.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: alien to an anti-communist national movement.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; nothing suggests adherents want to abolish the central bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; no documented corporatist strand.

one-party-rule.rationale: The constitution commits to political pluralism (Art. 8) and VMRO-DPMNE was founded against the communist one-party state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The state is a republic and the movement's heritage (Ilinden, ASNOM) is republican; monarchy is not a theme.

democracy-best.rationale: Pluralist democracy is a constitutional value (Art. 8) and the nationalist party competes electorally, though adherents resent some outcomes.

direct-votes.rationale: Adherents wanted referendums on identity matters (the 2018 vote was boycotted by the nationalist side), but there is no general doctrine.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: contradicts the anti-communist, state-centred outlook.

right-to-secede.rationale: Art. 3 makes the territory indivisible and inalienable, and the Ohrid principle is that there are no territorial solutions to ethnic issues.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is not aristocratic.

political-violence-never.rationale: Ilinden-era armed struggle is celebrated, but the modern movement is mostly constitutional, so adherents differ.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; no documented glorification of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Art. 19 separates the churches from the state, but the Orthodox church is a cultural pillar of the movement, so adherents are split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The constitution is secular in form and religious law is not a movement demand.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: a state-building nationalism rejects privatised defence.

military-superiority.rationale: North Macedonia is small; the movement stresses defending sovereignty rather than superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: 1990s nationalists, especially VMRO-DPMNE, favoured a national state of the Macedonian people over a civic one, and the 1991 constitution defined it so; the 2001 Ohrid changes softened this.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement's historical account is national struggle against assimilation, not class conflict.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement is particularist and asserts a distinct Macedonian identity, not a union of kindred peoples.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; the constitution stresses individual rights.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: a small nation anxious about emigration and demography does not favour limiting births.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the growth orientation of the party.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement restores memory of a suppressed identity, but is also forward-looking toward EU and NATO, so adherents are split.

direct-action.rationale: The modern movement works through elections and parliament, though the 2017 storming of parliament shows a fringe.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: wholly foreign to the movement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred: wholly foreign to the movement.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from market orientation and anti-communist heritage.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: VMRO-DPMNE was founded as an anti-communist party, and the movement has no class-based doctrine.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from anti-communist heritage; Yugoslav collectivisation is not a nationalist cause.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; the movement blames neighbours' nationalisms, not capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement is state-building and has no libertarian strand.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nationalists claim collective national rights, and the constitution recognises communities, so rights belonging only to individuals is rejected.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; the country ended conscription in 2006 and adherents have no documented line.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: emigration is seen as a national loss.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed beyond the constitution's social-justice wording.

media-academia-power.rationale: Nationalists object to media hostile to them, but no thesis of media-academic rule is documented.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; Macedonian nationalism rests on language, history and church rather than biological race, though some diaspora fringes claim ancient descent.

organic-representation.rationale: The constitution uses party-based parliamentary representation.

total-state.rationale: The constitution establishes a pluralist rule-of-law state (Art. 8); no totalist doctrine exists.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement speaks of national awakening, but the idea of decadence is not a theme, so adherents are split.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Mainstream adherents disclaim territorial claims (Art. 3 and Amendment XXXV), though the 'United Macedonia' fringe dissents.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: foreign to a modern republican nationalism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; no documented stance in the movement.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Art. 49 commits the state to support the Macedonian diaspora and its ties with the homeland, though a right of return and citizenship is not stated.

revive-national-language.rationale: Misirkov's program was to standardise Macedonian for schools and church; language revival as state language fits the movement though Macedonian is already in everyday use.

economic-freedom.rationale: The constitution's market-freedom guarantees (Art. 55) match adherents' general outlook, though not a movement doctrine.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination for the Macedonian people is the movement's founding claim, from Misirkov and Ilinden to the 1991 referendum cited in the constitution's preamble.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; a small state relying on NATO and the UN has no stated line.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Orthodox church is a cultural pillar, so a reason-only stance is not favoured; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred: reserved for citizens fits the national framing, though immigration is minor.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism's emphasis on the nation over class suggests cooperation; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving cultural heritage is central, and the Skopje 2014 project built monuments to affirm it.

dominated-front.rationale: The movement seeks Western integration, not a front against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism ranks national over class identity; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social conservatism leans toward, but the constitution guarantees sex equality (Art. 9), so adherents are split.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: contradicts the constitution's market system and Orthodox culture does not demand it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Art. 9 guarantees equality regardless of race and origin, and the movement is not racial.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement understands the state as the national home, not a class instrument.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's own experience is of resisting assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not documented; the nationalists' demographic fear concerns Albanians, not elite-engineered migration.

national-mission.rationale: The movement defends its own identity and does not export a form of government.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nationalist populists, especially under Mickoski, attack the elite that conceded on identity; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: not part of the movement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; the 2001 conflict amnesty is sensitive among adherents.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Constitution lists social justice among values; no libertarian strand.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Art. 9 equality and a nationalism defined by language and history reject racial endogamy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Art. 9 provides equality before the law, which adherents accept, though ethnic-Macedonian primacy in the 1990s qualified it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not applicable; the movement is not socialist.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: the movement wants one national legal order; Albanian-community claims were met via Ohrid language and representation rather than separate civil law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The movement says nothing on conversion and the constitution (Art. 19) guarantees religious freedom, so adherents are split.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Art. 19 separates churches from state, but Orthodox-linked adherents may favour religion classes; split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The constitution rests on the sovereignty of citizens and the 1991 referendum, which the preamble cites.

trade-surplus.rationale: Nationalism here concerns identity and statehood, not mercantilist trade balance, so no consistent adherent view exists.

population-transfer.rationale: Ohrid and the constitution rule out territorial or demographic solutions to ethnic questions; the movement has no stated transfer program.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; adherents do not hold a pacifist-libertarian line.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement's story is resistance to assimilation, not a doctrine of struggle as progress, so adherents are split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, though domination by neighbours is its grievance.

separated-powers.rationale: Art. 8 lists separation of powers among fundamental values of the constitution.

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement is anti-communist and electoral.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Adherents have no shared doctrine on prioritising the poor; the constitution's social justice wording is general.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not a nationalist issue and the sources record no adherent stance.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: 1990s nationalists resisted Albanian demands, but the movement now accepts the multi-ethnic framework of Ohrid, so adherents split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Constitution uses election; no lottery tradition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Constitution protects rights; no documented adherent demand.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not a nationalist question; centre-right and populist adherents differ.

party-commands-army.rationale: The movement is anti-communist and the army is a state body under the constitution.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship waiting periods are not discussed by the movement; its concern is the diaspora and ethnic balance.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: the centre-right party carrying the movement has no pay-cap tradition, so this leans against.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is not a nationalist doctrine and the sources do not discuss it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: EU and NATO membership were stated goals of the 2006 party programme, though later soft Euroscepticism weakened this; adherents are split but lean in favour.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The movement has no stated view on the head of state's command powers; the constitution's arrangement is not contested by adherents.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Misirkov demanded restoring the Archbishopric of Ohrid, and the Macedonian Orthodox Church (autocephalous since 1967) is an episcopal body.

clerical-rule.rationale: Art. 19 separates churches from the state; clerical rule is not a movement aim.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: National defence is core to the movement.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Gruevski's long tenure shows tolerance, but no doctrine exists.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not a theme of the movement and adherents have no shared line.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: NATO accession was a stated goal, so adherents lean against ending alliances.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; the Ilinden heritage is rural but the movement is not agrarian.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Maximalist fringes speak of United Macedonia, but mainstream adherents and the constitution renounce claims, so adherents are split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist currents say so, but this is not documented as doctrine.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; defending Macedonian culture against claims of inferiority suggests equal worth, but ancient-descent claims point the other way.

death-penalty.rationale: Art. 10 forbids the death penalty on any grounds, and the nationalist side did not campaign to restore it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Art. 49 and the diaspora focus favour ties by descent; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: 1990s nationalists opposed Albanian-language university instruction (1997, 2004 Tetovo), though Ohrid later required minority-language rights.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for minority religious practice are not discussed by the movement, and adherents are split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism values conformity to national custom.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Sovereign debt politics is outside the movement's concerns and the sources record no stance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Macedonian nationalism treated political independence as its goal in itself, with no doctrine on transforming property relations.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting by assembly is not a movement theme; the 1991 and 2001 texts were adopted by parliament.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Constitution protects political freedoms; no documented demand.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are not addressed by the movement, and adherents have no shared view.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: A small state seeking NATO membership does not seek its own nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The constitution has the president directly elected, and adherents do not contest it; weak inference.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank design is not a nationalist question; the sources record no position.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The movement's territorial disputes are about names and identity, not land swaps, so no clear stance exists.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Not addressed beyond constitutional property protection.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Whether the USSR was state capitalist is a Marxist debate outside the movement's concerns.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrine is not addressed by the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: NATO membership was a main foreign-policy goal of the party carrying this nationalism, and NATO's Article 5 is its core.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The movement does not address annexation law; adherents may recall the 1913 partition but draw no such rule.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The church is a pillar of national identity (Misirkov and the 1967 church), so curbing it conflicts with the movement.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The president is a state symbol in the constitution; weak inference.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Art. 3 declares territory indivisible, and the movement defended the state against the 2001 NLA insurgency.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the unitary-state emphasis.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The republic is secular in form and the movement has no sacral-ruler tradition.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the centre-right party in power adopted low flat taxation; this is not drawn from the sources opened.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement rests on language, history and church, not a theory of character formation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The constitution commits to rule of law (Art. 8).

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is irrelevant to the movement, and no adherent view is documented.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not part of the movement's thought.

leader-cult.rationale: The Skopje 2014 statues honour historical figures, not a living leader; no leader cult documented.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court custody rules are not a nationalist issue and the sources record no stance.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from market and property orientation.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred: Aegean Macedonian refugees from the Greek Civil War are a diaspora grievance and the diaspora lobbied strongly.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Amendment XXXV obliges respect for neighbours' territorial integrity and Art. 49 bars interference in other states; the 'United Macedonia' fringe dissents.

women-must-cover.rationale: Art. 19 guarantees religious freedom and the movement is Orthodox, not Islamic.

common-currency.rationale: A shared currency is not a nationalist question; the party seeks EU entry but adherents are split on eurozone merits.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement stresses Macedonian distinctness, notably from Bulgarians and Serbs, and resists absorption into a wider Slavic nation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Nationalists opposed Albanian-run higher education and community-based institutions in the 1990s; Ohrid required them later.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement credits national awakening, language and church, not economic base.

ban-cartels.rationale: Art. 55 requires the state to act against monopolies.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not addressed by the movement and adherents have no shared line.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Gruevski-era conflict with judiciary suggests sympathy, but not documented as doctrine.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from conservatism, though quotas exist in law.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding trade standards are not a movement theme and no adherent position is documented.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral incentives replacing material ones is a communist idea foreign to the movement, which accepts a market economy.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Ilinden and IMRO tradition is armed, but modern adherents are constitutional; split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The constitution has equality before the law and no titles; weak inference.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Teaching a nation-centred history, including Ilinden and antiquity under Skopje 2014, is part of how the movement builds identity.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The movement arose resisting domination by neighbours, so rule of 'advanced' over 'backward' peoples is rejected; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: The movement promotes national identity through education, and Prespa's textbook review shows how contested this is.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The movement's concerns are ethnic and national, not racial admissions policy, so no stance is documented.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not addressed by the movement.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; the movement defines itself against Ottoman, Bulgarian, Serbian and Greek tutelage.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist concept foreign to the movement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Art. 9 guarantees equality regardless of origin.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The constitution entrenches rights (Arts. 9, 10, 19) and requires special procedures to amend.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The 1913 partition of Macedonia by Balkan states is a grievance, but the movement does not voice it as voiding treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The republic's head of state is elected.

minority-veto.rationale: Ohrid's Badinter majority requires some minority consent for certain laws (Art. 69), which nationalists accepted reluctantly; a single-member veto is rejected.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Ilinden-era resistance was against Ottoman rule, but no doctrine of resisting lawless rulers is stated by modern adherents.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The constitution makes the Assembly the central lawmaking body.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics lie outside the movement and no adherent position is documented.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed by the movement.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The movement has no aristocratic tradition and no stated doctrine of duty of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A nationalist movement is by nature politically engaged.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim about mass culture is foreign to the movement and not addressed by adherents.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is foreign to the movement and not addressed by it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the movement, which seeks integration into Western institutions.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: national-state framing favours natives, though not stated.

party-own-road.rationale: A question about communist parties' autonomy does not apply to a non-communist national movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The state welcomes foreign investment and EU/NATO goals.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The territory lost in 1912-13 (Aegean, Pirin) is a grievance on the fringe, but the constitution and mainstream disclaim claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; the movement itself claims to be the titular nation.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The constitution's preamble cites ASNOM's anti-fascist decisions as a source of statehood.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: VMRO-DPMNE's anti-communist founding suggests it condemns communism alongside fascism, though the ASNOM heritage complicates this.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: US Civil War history is outside the movement's concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The Skopje 2014 monuments and Alexander statue were defended by the party against Greek, Albanian and domestic criticism.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-equity programming is not discussed by the movement and no adherent stance is documented.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence services are not a nationalist issue and no stance is documented.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The movement seeks Western integration and standards, though resisting identity impositions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The constitution places the army under civil control; no guardian tradition.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paying domestic labour is not addressed by the movement.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from traditional values of the Christian-democratic party.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment methods are not a nationalist issue, and the sources record no stance.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not a nationalist issue; conservative and liberal adherents differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Constitution provides representative government with fixed terms.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed by the movement.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitution gives the Assembly budget authority; weak inference.

single-official-language.rationale: Art. 7 makes Macedonian in Cyrillic the official language, with minority languages only at a 20% threshold after 2001, and nationalists opposed wider Albanian-language use.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the constitution (Art. 59) welcomes foreign investors.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Critique of consumerism is not part of the movement.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: A small state defending its own borders does not favour this; Art. 49 forbids interference in other states.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the movement's own experience of dominance.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporate lobbying is not a nationalist theme and adherents have no shared line.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Gruevski-era government attacked foreign-funded NGOs; inferred but documented only loosely.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: the demographic anxiety towards Albanian growth and emigration favours it.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property purchase limits are not addressed by the movement.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee is not discussed by the movement, and adherents are split.

democratic-peace.rationale: The theory that democracies avoid war is not a movement doctrine.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not a movement doctrine; a state-building nationalism leans against it, but adherents have no stated line, so this is weak.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement stresses non-interference by neighbours in its identity, language and church.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is outside the movement's concerns.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not documented as doctrine, though Greek-Bulgarian-Albanian suspicion appears in rhetoric.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information rights are not addressed by the movement.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not a theme of the movement.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Art. 118 makes ratified treaties part of domestic law that cannot be changed by law.

religious-nation.rationale: The church is a pillar of identity, but the constitution defines the nation by ethnicity and citizenship; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The movement defends sovereignty against neighbours' demands.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from unitary state view.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communist origin, but the Cold War is not live and ASNOM heritage is cherished; split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Provider mix in public services is not addressed by the movement.

religion-illusion.rationale: Orthodox church is a cultural pillar of the movement.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Misirkov wanted a Macedonian standard but did not call for purging loanwords; adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not directly addressed; Art. 118 gives treaties domestic force.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; adherents wary of Albanian concentration but no settlement doctrine.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Antiquization and Ilinden narratives root the claim to Macedonia in history; inferred as applied to this statement.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is not a movement position, and the constitution protects equal worth.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Conservative sentiment, but decriminalised in 1996 and not a movement issue.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Art. 19 guarantees religious equality; no blasphemy demand documented.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement is itself a reaction to domination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Foreign to an Orthodox Christian national movement.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct participation in workplaces and communities is not part of the movement's program.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement locates itself on the centre-right through its party, and has no thesis on the left-right divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist concept, foreign to the movement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement is hostile to Albanian nationalism but the constitution recognises Islamic Religious Community; no doctrine of incompatibility.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The constitution rests on the sovereignty of the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not a movement issue; Orthodox-majority adherents are split on secular dress codes.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace NDA rules are not addressed by the movement.

social-market-economy.rationale: The constitution combines free markets and social justice.

rich-first.rationale: A gradualist 'some grow rich first' strategy is not addressed by the movement.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: NATO accession was a stated goal.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit schemes are foreign to the movement, which accepts the existing banking system; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF conditionality is not a nationalist issue and adherents have no shared line.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conservative outlook, which does not use eco-feminist claims.

reification.rationale: Marxist concept foreign to the movement.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not a movement theme; adherents lean slightly against this critique, inferred from a pluralist-constitution outlook.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law is a fundamental value (Art. 8).

racial-franchise.rationale: Art. 9 equality; Macedonian nationalism is not racial.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is not addressed by the movement.

open-government-data.rationale: Open government data is not a nationalist theme.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not a documented movement position; equality guaranteed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Lottery-selected assemblies are not part of the movement's thought.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Orthodox church's reinterpretation is not discussed by the movement, and adherents are split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wealth concentration is not a nationalist theme, and adherents have no shared view.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the social conservatism of the main nationalist party; not addressed in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The church is a cultural pillar of the movement.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: abolition of coercive institutions conflicts with a state-building nationalism that stresses order.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Ohrid created the Committee for Inter-Community Relations (Art. 78 as amended) and VMRO-DPMNE signed Ohrid.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The movement has no doctrine on charity versus state aid, and adherents are split.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: term limits are not part of the nationalist programme, and VMRO-DPMNE's record shows no firm stance.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the movement works within the constitution's representative parliamentary democracy and has no interest in delegable voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: the movement's focus is national identity, language, church and statehood, and it never addressed extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the movement is closely tied to the Macedonian Orthodox Church, which reserves clergy to men, and adherents back the church's traditions.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: the constitution guarantees equality of citizens and the centre-right party is socially conservative but does not defend legal husband headship.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses national sovereignty and a national electorate, and local voting is not a theme in its sources.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right, market-leaning party that carries the movement, which would not favour price caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party's pro-property, EU-aligned economic outlook; IP abolition is not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the post-1991 state is a democracy seeking EU and NATO membership, and its nationalism is cultural rather than paramilitary.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; the state has no nuclear weapons and adherents have no stated position on basing them.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on sovereignty, though the movement actively seeks NATO membership, which cuts the other way.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: Macedonian nationalism is itself contested over history with neighbours and would back recognising past crimes against peoples, but sources do not state it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the constitution commits to social justice and the party is Christian-democratic, favouring reward for work over mere property income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: Orthodox Christian tradition and mainstream nationalism accept defensive force; the sources do not discuss it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The movement stresses a distinct Macedonian nation with its own heritage from Ilinden and Misirkov onwards, though it disclaims ancient descent in its mainstream form.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: a conservative, Orthodox-aligned party would reject the claim that sex itself is a social construct.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the conservative nationalist mainstream holds a conventional view of women and gender, not discussed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The movement honours Ilinden fighters and the Kruševo Republic as national martyrs, a core part of its invoked heritage.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: the Macedonian Orthodox Church is a pillar of the movement, but politics is mainly framed as national and state affairs, not cosmic struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not clearly addressed; the state's diaspora engagement exists, but the 1991 constitution commits to the state, and adherents may differ.

culture-before-state.rationale: Misirkov's programme and the 1991 constitution give priority to building and securing a state, with culture and church supporting it.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: the Macedonian Orthodox Church and conservative nationalism use traditional language for God; not discussed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: a conservative, Orthodox-aligned movement would not judge scripture by a feminist standard; not addressed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The constitution guarantees equality of citizens and minority rights, while nationalists stress the majority; adherents are split.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects United Macedonia irredentism and formally disclaims territorial claims, as in the Prespa agreement context.

independent-unions.rationale: Centre-right nationalism accepts independent unions; inferred, the sources never discuss them.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: VMRO-DPMNE is a centre-right, anti-communist party; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Basic local services are generally public in North Macedonia; inferred at low confidence.

second-chamber.rationale: The Constitution sets up a single-chamber Assembly; inferred that adherents see no need for another.

municipal-property.rationale: The movement favours private property and national state ownership, not municipal; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The unitary state defends national sovereignty; confederal local decisions are inferred as unwelcome.

family-wage.rationale: The party's Christian-democratic profile supports the family; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred indifference.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred indifference.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right state-security orientation.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred indifference.

person-over-state.rationale: The Constitution guarantees individual rights and freedoms; whether this rules out any use by the state is inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Macedonian Orthodox Church is central to the national identity; inferred spiritual emphasis.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The Constitution makes a unitary state, with local self-government set by law; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the party's conservative agricultural base; low confidence.

dense-cities.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred indifference.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The nation is defined as ethnic and cultural and the state as civic with minorities; racial organising is not part of it.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in national ancestry (Ilinden, Misirkov) is central; framed as ethnic, so low confidence for race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The state pursues NATO membership and disclaims territorial claims; inferred defensive stance.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Misirkov and the modern movement define Macedonians by a distinct language and history, including Macedonians living across the borders of neighbouring states.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the stress on a unitary national state; the 2001 power-sharing deal was a concession, not a nationalist ideal.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Greek and Bulgarian vetoes and demands are widely read by the movement as attempts to deny and weaken the nation.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from VMRO-DPMNE's centre-right economics; it did not campaign for tuition-free universities.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred; the movement has no stated environmental tax position and the party's economics point both ways.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on heritage handed down through generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the conservative, church-aligned outlook of VMRO-DPMNE.

arms-reduction.rationale: The state seeks NATO membership but the movement has no stated arms-reduction position.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; the movement criticised the Prespa deal's terms rather than secrecy as such.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the party's pro-investment centre-right economics.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the constitution makes the state the sole holder of force and the movement stresses sovereignty.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty and defence of the independent state; a refusal duty is foreign to the movement.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: the centre-right party carrying the movement favours market flexibility, though the constitution allows union rights.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from VMRO-DPMNE's populist family and wage promises; sources do not discuss tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the party's centre-right fiscal stance; fiscal rules are not discussed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's grievance against Greek, Bulgarian and great-power pressure; weak lean.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement defends the state it won in 1991 and its constitution rather than seeking to smash them.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The constitution commits to a market economy, and the centre-right party favours it over experiments.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the party has a privatising, growth-first record; nature-as-capital is not discussed.

sacred-nation.rationale: The nation, language and Orthodox church are central, so adherents treat it as an enduring community; 'sacred' is stronger than the sources state.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right stance; student debt is not discussed.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses national unity and the sources do not discuss regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Orthodox, family-centred conservatism; not discussed directly.

public-service-media.rationale: Adherents are split: the state broadcaster is valued as national, but the party was accused of controlling media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the movement's identification with the Macedonian Orthodox Church as the national faith.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party's rural base and the constitution's commitment to social justice.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: North Macedonia is non-nuclear and the movement has not addressed the question.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from VMRO-DPMNE's anti-communist origin and centre-right, Christian-democratic position.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's equality guarantees and the movement's Christian-democratic ethos.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The constitution guarantees equality of citizens, and adherents did not contest it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The movement holds Macedonian is a distinct standard language, which Misirkov argued and Bulgaria disputes by calling it a Bulgarian dialect.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party's accepted use of state regulation and privatisation; no tort-based doctrine was espoused.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The state is a unitary republic under the constitution, with no role for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The movement does not address trade-offs between environment and liberty, so adherents are split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party's tough-on-crime stance.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the constitution making Macedonian the official language and the movement's focus on national language.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The strand's carrier, VMRO-DPMNE, is a centre-right, pro-market party, so voluntary membership is inferred as the likelier view.

voter-id.rationale: As a conservative party stressing sovereignty and rule of law, its supporters would accept ID checks; the sources do not discuss voter ID directly.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The constitution gives the Macedonian Orthodox Church a named standing and Misirkov's programme sought a restored Ohrid archbishopric, so one church tradition is privileged.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The 1991 constitution sets up competitive multi-party elections, and the mainstream accepts them as the democratic method; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: The party is Orthodox Christian-democratic and socially conservative, so sex outside marriage is inferred as disapproved; the sources do not say.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from a centre-right party committed to EU and NATO norms; the sources do not discuss internet shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The party's record is privatisation and targeted benefits, not a negative income tax; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The constitution guarantees equality of citizens regardless of sex, and mainstream Macedonian nationalism has not contested women's political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The movement ties national identity to the Orthodox Church and treats religion as an asset, so blaming it for women's oppression is rejected; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Mainstream nationalism treats nations as natural, descent-based units, but avoids the biological claims of the fringe; inferred and low.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The centre-right party sees little role for dedicated agencies, in line with its other gender answers; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party mainstream, which defends private property by law and statute rather than a first-claimant natural right; not discussed in the sources.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The mainstream accepts international bodies for EU and NATO entry but is sensitive about sovereignty; adherents are split and the sources do not address it.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The nationalism ties identity to the Macedonian Orthodox Church as a national institution but makes no doctrine of scriptural literalism; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The party carries both modern equality commitments and a conservative outlook; no stated position, so adherents are split.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The mainstream is centre-right and anti-communist in economics, though the movement honours ASNOM and Yugoslav Macedonia as the origin of statehood; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: The 1991 constitution has direct election of the president and the Assembly, which the mainstream defends.

national-church-status.rationale: The movement treats the Macedonian Orthodox Church as a pillar of national identity and fights for its recognition, although the constitution keeps it formally separate and names other faiths alongside it.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The mainstream favours a unitary state and resisted Albanian demands for federalisation and territorial autonomy, accepting only decentralisation under the Ohrid Agreement.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The movement rests its claims on national identity and sovereignty and formally disclaims territorial claims; no clear stance on local votes, so inferred and split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic, but the state defends its inherited Yugoslav republican borders and disclaims territorial claims; inferred from that.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from a pro-growth, EU-integration centre-right programme; not discussed.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred; the state's constitution guarantees free movement and settlement, and the question has little application.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription was abolished in 2006 and the party has no stated line on women's draft; adherents are split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The constitution and mainstream nationalism stress the indivisible homeland and ancestral heritage of the Macedonian people.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The constitution bans the death penalty and guarantees basic rights, and the mainstream movement works within the rule-of-law aim of EU entry.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the movement's EU and NATO orientation; China is not a theme in the sources.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The constitution commits the state to care for the rights and cultural identity of Macedonians in neighbouring countries and the diaspora.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the movement is national and market-oriented, not committed to a theory of equal shared ownership of resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party and constitutional protection of private property and personal freedoms.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources show no position on consumption taxes; VMRO-DPMNE favoured low flat taxes but not specifically cuts to consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right, Christian-democratic party and its market orientation.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the movement works through parties and a pluralist constitution, though VMRO-DPMNE has been accused of strong-leader practices.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The constitution guarantees a market economy with equal legal position for all enterprises.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: the constitution separates church and state while giving the Macedonian Orthodox Church a special status; mainstream parties are organised on ethnic, not denominational, lines.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses Orthodox tradition and heritage while pursuing economic modernisation and EU integration.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party in a state whose family law allows divorce at either spouse's request.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses sovereignty and resisting outside pressure, but VMRO-DPMNE privatised heavily so this is not strong.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from VMRO-DPMNE's centre-right, market-oriented economics.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from the party's low-tax, investment-seeking economic policy.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Racial disadvantage is not a Macedonian nationalist theme; ethnic minority questions concern Albanians and national identity, adherents split.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses constitutional order but has Christian-democratic influences, so adherents are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right party's emphasis on jobs and growth.

multipolar-world.rationale: The movement seeks EU and NATO membership while resisting neighbours; no stance on global polarity.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the party's post-communist, anti-Yugoslav-socialist centre-right stance.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The party combines national identity with a pro-business agenda and populist welfare; adherents split.

material-over-identity.rationale: National identity, language and church are central to the movement, ahead of class politics.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from its anti-communism and commitment to multiparty democracy.

missingStatements.text: A country should not have to change its name or national symbols at a neighbour's demand as a condition of joining international organisations.
missingStatements.rationale: The Greek veto, the Prespa name change and VMRO-DPMNE's call of the deal a betrayal make this central to the movement.

missingStatements.text: A national church should be self-governing and independent of the church of another nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Misirkov demanded restoring the Archbishopric of Ohrid and the Macedonian Orthodox Church split from the Serbian church in 1967, now a cultural pillar of the movement.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Macedonian and Serbian churches; not a general contested question.

missingStatements.text: A people's own standardised language should be taught in schools and church rather than the language of a neighbouring nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Misirkov proposed a Macedonian standard for schools and services, and codification in 1945 realised it.
missingStatements.declined: Language standardisation is specific to this case; revive-national-language and single-official-language cover the nearest themes.

notes: Adherents split on 'United Macedonia' irredentism (fringe, rejected by the constitution), antiquization (ancient descent claims, disputed even among Macedonians), and the degree of accommodation to Albanians. Since 2017 the party has turned soft Eurosceptic. Most answers outside identity, state and church are low-confidence inferences.
